The Sony Datacollecting is ofc. BS

Genneral:
The Game runs really well, and I haven't had issues yet. Its allso not too taxing and I expect it will run pretty well on older hardware. I think this is one of the best ports i have seen in a long time.
At the same time the game is very pretty and it could really have come out yesterday. The only part of this that seems aged is the facial animations that are very stiff.

Story:
The world building is great and the intro of the main protagainst Aloy i think is great.
Sadly at the end of the first act. She becomes "The Choosen one" and i really feel a little bit of a letdown on this, and there are some, for my part, eye rolling moments. But i guess it is not as bad as say the 3. new Tomb Raider game.
The voice acting is all in all good and allthough a bit on the forgetable side i do like the characters in genneral. 
And as i said in the beginning the facial animations are very stiff and the lip syncing really looks like a 2010 game, i dont normally care about this but its kinda dragging me out of the story

- The game uses "boonfire" saves, combined with quick saves so i do see a senario where you run out of resources in a nasty fight and will have to go way back to start again.

I dont mind the idea but the execution is extremely tedious

Absolutely great game. I beat it on the lowest tier of steam deck, and no performance issues. Has a great story, great combat, great graphics, and is a great game. I do not regret buying. 10/10

Yes, yes, absolutely yes. The game plays perfectly fine, fast, nice and stable. The studio porting it to PC did an amazing job. It plays even better than the PS4 version of it. It feels like the game was meant for PC. I'm happy replaying this game now. You don't really need the remastered version upgrade to make it look a bit "better", the game has plenty of eyecandy on its own but if you don't like it, you can always upgrade. Highly recommended to play this.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe mouse and keyboard controls as feeling lazy or poorly adapted, noting features like unmappable controls and having to cycle through items as if using a d-pad.

citations.review_text:
Main complaint is I don't like the combat controls. Third person action games of this sort don't usually have a lot of aiming and shooting, but this one does. That creates a problem: use the gamepad or mouse and keyboard? For me, trying to aim in a shooter with a gamepad is frustrating and hard, even with time-slowdown. This is fixed if you play with a mouse and keyboard. However, now the melee is hard to manage. This is primarily because the mouse and keyboard implementation is lazy. Controls can't be remapped, and rather than design the controls for the mouse and keyboard it just substitutes for the gamepad. For example, rather than having the number keys directly map to items, you have to cycle left and right as if your keyboard was a d-pad.

The game is somewhat woke. How is it in a remote tribal village, somewhat themed on Viking culture, you   have every race represented for no apparent reason? And the developers noticeably went out of their way to make most of the leaders and heroes all minorities of some sort or another.

It's also hard to see the protagonist in a positive light once you start killing humans instead of machines. I can see killing people who clearly did wrong according to the story, or in games that present some kind of wartime situation. But are soon slaughtering people in the hundreds, all white men by the way. For some reason representation wasn't important suddenly. I understand bandits are bad people but the brutality gets ridiculous. You speak as if you were this kind-hearted girl, who just happened to be drenched in blood 10 minutes ago.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that facial animations during conversations look ridiculous.

citations.review_text:
Graphics is good, but the facial animations are ridiculous.  Combat is mostly good, but is repetitive against some of the bigger enemies.   Story is good at the beginning and near the end.  Didn't finish the DLC.  Someday. "climbing" is stupid.

7/10

This game (and series as a whole) definitely has a reputation of being behind the pack compared to other popular open-world RPGs made by other studios like CD PROJEKT RED, Bethesda, or FromSoftware. Most people agree that's it a good game but people don't sing it's praises as much.

I'll get the strongest aspect of the game out of the way: its gameplay. More than most other non-FromSoftware open-world RPGs, this game relies on the player using tactics other than just running straight into combat. Even at higher levels, you're disincentivized to strike with just your spear or regular arrows, as you'll get two or three shot even at Normal difficulty. Instead, you're expected to rely on stealth or equipment you've crafted beforehand - specialized arrows, bombs, ropes, etc. Each enemy also have specific weaknesses that can be tough to exploit at first, but become a breeze as you get used to the game's satisfying movement and systems. It's a very satisfying game to play overall, one that rewards you for your preparation and thinking. The game looks great and sounds great, too.

Now, unfortunately, the game's main issue is quite a big one - its story and world. It feels very impersonal, mostly due to how generic the main character, Aloy, is. An RPG lead being bland isn't an uncommon nor bad thing necessarily, but Aloy has just enough of a background in this world and dialogue in this story to be hard to project yourself unto while not having enough of a personality to be fun to follow around. This affects everything else, as well - because you don't identify with the main character, her interactions with NPCs and the world overall feels disconnected. On paper, the world of Horizon should be interesting - a post-apocalyptic world where hostile automatons roam it, and it is interesting sometimes with the robot designs and such. But it's kinda hard to really get into it 'cuz you're interacting with it through Aloy. Story is also overall kinda bland and predictable.

It…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that missing the power cell inside Mother's Watch before leaving requires waiting until later in the game to regain access to the area.

citations.review_text:
forced cut scenes, game is slow to pickup if it does at all, needed to modify settings to keep from getting motion sickness. It is not a fast paced game.  Mounts are only useful in certain situations, better to just fast travel everywhere.
If you do play, work on increasing your bag space for resources, keep the weapons as you need them for different situations, only sell when you upgrade the exact weapon. Kill the small creatures as you need the items they drop to upgrade/craft and purchase items. 

Note: if you leave Mother's Watch before getting the power cell inside, you have to wait towards later in the game to gain access again.

Loved this game. There are so many good things and a few bad things but overall would recommend this to people who like FarCry style games, killing baddies, taking over territories etc. The voice acting was superb in this game, the writing for the main story was also fantastic. I could have watched this as a movie instead of playing it, very well crafted. Loads of little tidbits you can pickup throughout the world. BUT after 72hrs it was getting old. The usual lets make a beautiful world, and drop poi's all over the map, we will make about 6 or 7 different types and just scatter them everywhere this will extend the gameplay of completionists. I am kind of funny where in the beginning I love this style of play because I think secretly I long to be a hoarder and this style of gaming allows me to collect without really taking up space. However after awhile it gets tedious especially when there is no real pay off for doing it other than to explore the world.

This brings me to my other point that I didn't like about this game. I am a wanderer so when I see an open map with fast travel checkpoints I think "oh I should just go unlock all those so future missions will be easy" Which led me to the part I didn't like which was the game felt unbalanced but only because I was jumping ahead. Once I went back to the main mission after realizing I had leveled up to 20 or so I realized the missions were only level 8. Once I stuck to the main missions the game felt better paced. But this is one of those games where yes it is an open world but it plays better when you follow the linear path the devs set out.

There were times too where the combat felt unbalanced, some machines were easy to take down and others were almost impossible. I also found the weapons system was a bit clunky, you had lots of options but once you leveled up enough you could just brute force your way through most situations.

Having said all that I really enjoyed this game and the story alone is worth a p…

Horizon Zero Dawn Complete Edition is an absolute triumph of an open-world action RPG. The game pairs fantastic graphics, featuring vibrant post-apocalyptic landscapes and terrifyingly detailed machine creatures, with a very compelling storyline that keeps you hooked as you uncover the mystery of humanity's downfall alongside Aloy. Packed with satisfying tactical combat and the included The Frozen Wilds expansion, it offers incredible value and is an easy, highly recommended pickup for anyone who loves story-driven adventures.

Combat allows you to go stealth, strat set-ups, or just run in guns ablazing. Story is good, kept me interested and excited for what was to come next. DLC was a bit underwhelming tbh. Overall I had fun with the game but I started feeling major burnout and decided I have no interest in finishing the DLC or chasing other achievements. Combat woes.... I felt that my arrows would shoot through enemies, and this was happening frequently. Even when they were stunned or I was using slow mo, my arrows would straight up miss even though the crosshairs were centered.

movement woes.... Climbing and jumping ledges would not always connect. The pole jumps was notoriously the worst. This game was obviously designed for console, which is why i'm not too hell bent on this. But the mount riding experience was absolute ♥♥♥♥♥ on PC. The movement might have been one of the worst for a AAA game i've ever experienced.

Liked the story, world building and combat. Voice acting was good.
Open world seemed a little empty in places and I was expecting a bit more variety in the machines.
Traveling on a mount did not feel great so I ended up walking everywhere.
Overall a solid game.

[h2]Horizon Zero Dawn – Complete Edition[/h2]

[b]Keywords:[/b] Single Player • Open World • Action RPG • Exploration • Sci-Fi • Post-Apocalyptic • Combat • Story Driven • Hunting • Speedrun Community

[b]Overview[/b]

✔ Massive, beautifully designed open world
✔ Unique machine-hunting combat system
✔ Strong main story with engaging world mystery
✔ Complete Edition includes full expansion content

[b]What’s Good[/b]

✔ Extremely satisfying combat focused on weak points and strategy
✔ Incredible world design with varied and memorable regions
✔ Great progression system with skills, gear, and upgrades
✔ Strong replay value thanks to builds and challenge runs
✔ Excellent speedrun community with active strategies and optimized routes

[b]Exploration[/b]

✔ Diverse environments from forests to deserts to ancient ruins
✔ Hidden lore and collectibles that reward curiosity
✔ Side quests that expand the world meaningfully

[b]Game play Feel[/b]

Combat is tactical and rewarding, especially when mastering different weapon types against machines. Exploration constantly feels worthwhile, and progression keeps the experience fresh from start to finish.

[b]Final Verdict[/b]

If you enjoy open-world RPGs with deep combat systems, strong exploration, and a very active speedrun community, Horizon Zero Dawn – Complete Edition is an outstanding experience.

[b]10/10 – A visually stunning and highly replayable open-world masterpiece with a great community.[/b]

[b]Reviewer's PC Specs:[/b]
Linux: Arch with Hyprland
CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 3600X 6-Core Processor
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT
VRAM: 8 GB
RAM: 31 GB

claims.claim: Reviewers report that tutorial quests must be manually activated to track progress.

citations.review_text:
Note: This version is delisted; you will need the Remastered version.

[h2]Getting Started[/h2]

This game is a slow burn that took me three years and several attempts before it clicked. Master the systems early: if you just fire arrows at robo-dinosaurs they will kill you. The game wants you to use its toolkit. So do all the tutorials.

Note: You must manually activate tutorial quests for them to track progress. A poor design decision.

[h2]Story & Design [/h2]

The core sci-fi narrative is solid, featuring an affecting performance and animation for young Aloy. 

While the main arc builds real stakes, it culminates in a lackluster final confrontation. The world is also cluttered with "busy-work" fetch quests and errands for people I didn't care about, offering mostly worthless rewards. Sadly, they are required for 100% achievements.

Visually, the world is incredible and vast, and the combat is addictive. The audio deserves every award it received. 

However, interiors are a disappointment, reusing drab, samey textures. Cutscene quality is variable.

The Remastered version addresses some of these issues.

[h2]Performance[/h2]

This is a stellar PC port with only one crash in 110 hours. The Decima engine (also used by Death Stranding) renders vast distances with minimal pop-in even on moderate hardware. The lighting is superb, although weather and time-of-day transitions are often too abrupt.

[h2]Ideology, Feminism, Poison[/h2]

The game is a deeply sexist, toxic feminist power fantasy wrapped in "strong woman" marketing.

Despite depicting a matriarchal society where men are the primary defenders, the game regularly reminds us that women have it harder. Aloy feels less like a tribal outcast and more like a 21st-century asexual progressive in a man's role.

The game's core premise is that women create, nurture and heal while men destroy. 

Women are portrayed as reliable and earnest,  their only "flaws" being stubbornness or over-zealousness. Meanwhile, men are fre…

Thoroughly enjoyed the Complete Edition even when Remastered was just getting released.  Not sure why they're selling remastered editions only 7.5 years after the original!  Fight me but; as someone who played the OG DOOM + Half-Life, the original graphics are both great and easier on a graphics card I plan to keep for 10 years.  Either way, this game does a fantastic job of stealth into brute force while still having more strategy than reflex skill.

Anyway, on to negligible spoiler tips for completionists:
I played on Normal, supposedly you can lower it mid-game.  No urgency for any quests (despite them being like "tomorrow night" constantly).  Mild fall damage.
Get Silent Strike and Lure skills ASAP.  Use it to lure the early enemies to tall grass where you get a free kill for shards.  Until I did this, I couldn't keep up making arrows fast enough!
Pulling back on your shot increases accuracy, not damage; quick fire when close.
You can upgrade your own capacity from the same menu as your inventory/quests/etc.  Just grind it all out from the starting areas! citations.review_text:
This game had massive potential, with excellent stealth, but it was frankly ruined for me by the scripted fail, infinite enemies nonsense of the “Revenge of the Nora” mission, in which you are automatically detected, no matter what, no matter how perfectly stealthy you were, after killing a certain number of enemies.

Frankly, being detected when I wasn't detected, ruins my immersion. I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone.

Additionally, the amount of unnatural, irrational roadblocks to platform climbing in Frozen Wilds is also immersion-breaking, and, frankly, stupidly unnecessary. It's really just there to make you walk the long way around, because it'll tell you that you 'cannot enter this location.'

What is really means is 'we want you to walk 3,500 metres more than you have to because we hate you for being smart enough to figure out how to climb the wall instead.' It breaks my immersion for being on playing a protagonist who lived her whole life in the mountains.

More than that, the Frozen Wilds has tons of things THAT YOU ARE SUPPOSED TO CLIMB. So they're punishing you for being smart enough to climb without those things, in a lot of locations, but just having Sue Storm sit there blocking you pointlessly.

Also, certain tutorial quests can glitch and not advance despite performing the action instructed and with the weapon it is a tutorial for. The initial Rattler is a good example of this, but there are others, and it can be really annoying.

Note: This version is delisted; you will need the Remastered version.

[h2]Getting Started[/h2]

This game is a slow burn that took me three years and several attempts before it clicked. Master the systems early: if you just fire arrows at robo-dinosaurs they will kill you. The game wants you to use its toolkit. So do all the tutorials.

Note: You must manually activate tutorial quests for them to track progress. A poor design decision.

[h2]Story & Design [/h2]

The core sci-fi narrative is solid, featuring an affecting performance and animation for young Aloy. 

While the main arc builds real stakes, it culminates in a lackluster final confrontation. The world is also cluttered with "busy-work" fetch quests and errands for people I didn't care about, offering mostly worthless rewards. Sadly, they are required for 100% achievements.

Visually, the world is incredible and vast, and the combat is addictive. The audio deserves every award it received. 

However, interiors are a disappointment, reusing drab, samey textures. Cutscene quality is variable.

The Remastered version addresses some of these issues.

[h2]Performance[/h2]

This is a stellar PC port with only one crash in 110 hours. The Decima engine (also used by Death Stranding) renders vast distances with minimal pop-in even on moderate hardware. The lighting is superb, although weather and time-of-day transitions are often too abrupt.

[h2]Ideology, Feminism, Poison[/h2]

The game is a deeply sexist, toxic feminist power fantasy wrapped in "strong woman" marketing.

Despite depicting a matriarchal society where men are the primary defenders, the game regularly reminds us that women have it harder. Aloy feels less like a tribal outcast and more like a 21st-century asexual progressive in a man's role.

The game's core premise is that women create, nurture and heal while men destroy.
